summary: Eisei Kojima is a Buddhist studies scholar. In 1976, he was attested as a professor at Ryukoku University and president of Doho University.

Eishu Miyazaki (1913–1997) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (~1933–1938) and under Gyoo Kageyama. He held posts at Rissho University (~1949–1984) and Minobusan University (~1978–1986).
Eishun Fushimi works in the fields of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Hamburg (attested 1998) under David P. Jackson.
Eiyin Yasuda (born 1938) is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Ryukoku University (~1957–1961) and under Gyōin Hashimoto.
Eizan Tatsuta (1893–1979) was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Sokatsu Shaku. He founded Ningen Zen Kyodan.

Ekai Kawaguchi (1866–1945) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at institutions including Toyo University, Sera Monastery, and Central Hindu College under several teachers. His posts included rector at Gohyaku Rakan-ji (~1891) and professor at Toyo University (1916).
Eki Nakayama works in Buddhist studies and Indology. In 2020, he was attested as a student at Kyoto University and a DC2 special researcher at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science.
Ekkyo Uno is a Buddhist studies scholar. He held attested posts as a lecturer at Osaka University of Foreign Studies (1991) and as a non-regular researcher at Honganji Sōgakuin (1998).

Eleanor Nesbitt (born 1951) is a religious studies and Indology scholar who studied at Girton College, Cambridge, and the University of Oxford. She held a post at the University of Warwick (~1989–2012), where she became emerita professor in Education Studies.

Eleanor Rosch (born 1938) works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. She studied at Reed College and Harvard University under Roger Brown, and held posts at Brown University (~1969–1971) and as professor of cognitive psychology at UC Berkeley starting in 1971.

Elena De Rossi Filibeck is a Tibetology scholar who studied at the University of Rome under Luciano Petech (~1967–1971). She held posts at the University of Bonn (~1974–1977) and as associate professor at the University of Rome (1980).
Elena France Hanson works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She earned her Doctor of Philosophy at Harvard University, studying under doctoral supervisor Charles Hallisey.

Elena Mucciarelli is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Tübingen (~2010–2013). She held posts at the University of Tübingen (2016–2017) and the University of Groningen (2020) as assistant professor and Gonda Lecturer.

Eli Franco (born 1953) is an Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tel Aviv University, EPHE, Paris Nanterre, and Hamburg. He held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences, University of Vienna, and chair of Indology at Leipzig (2004–2021).

Elijah Sacvan Ary (born 1972) is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Sera Monastery, INALCO, and Harvard University under Janet Gyatso, Leonard van der Kuijp, Charles Hallisey, and Geshe Karma Sonam.

Eliot Deutsch (1931–2020) was a philosophy and Indology scholar educated at Wisconsin, Chicago, Harvard, and Columbia. He held posts at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute (1960–1967) and as professor at the University of Hawaiʻi (1967–2006).

Elisa Freschi (born 1977) is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under Raffaele Torella. She held positions at the University of Rome (~2006–2012), the Austrian Academy of Sciences (2012), and the University of Vienna (~2017).

Elisabeth Schüssler Fiorenza (born 1938) is a religious studies scholar educated at Würzburg and Münster. She held professorships at Notre Dame (1970–1984), Episcopal Divinity School (1984–1988), and Harvard University (from 1988), and served as SBL president (1987–1988).

Elizabeth A. Cecil (born 1981) works in Indology, religious studies, and history/archaeology. She studied at Hastings College, Tennessee, and Brown University. She has held posts at Groningen, Leiden, and as assistant professor of religion at Florida State University (attested 2021).

Elizabeth Anne Morrison is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. She studied under Bernard Faure, Carl Bielefeldt, Janet Gyatso, and Susan Niditch, and held posts at Amherst College (1998–1999) and Middlebury College (attested 2008).
